title: Growth of Human and Sheep Corneal Endothelial Cell Layers on Biomaterial Membranes
protocol: Sterilize two pairs of number 4 watchmaker forceps by soaking them in a solution of 70% ethanol for 5 min or by autoclaving.
Prepare 100 mL of culture medium containing Opti-MEM 1 (1x) + GlutaMAX-1, 5% fetal bovine serum and 100 U/mL Pen/Strep.
Supplement the human corneal endothelial cell cultures with 50 µg/mL bovine pituitary extract, 0.08% chondroitin sulphate, 200 µg/mL calcium chloride and 0.3 mM L-ascorbic acid 2-phosphate.
Store the prepared culture medium in the dark at 4 °C for two weeks.
Coat the wells of a 6-well tissue culture plate with Attachment Factor according to the manufacturer's instructions.
Add 1 mL of culture medium to each coated well, preparing one well for each cornea.
Place the cornea, endothelium side up, into a sterile Petri dish on the stage of a dissecting microscope.
Adjust the illumination to well-light the corneal surface with sufficient contrast to highlight the endothelial layer.
Adjust the zoom so that the edge and some central corneal endothelium is in view.
Use sterilized watchmaker forceps to gently lift and tear Descemet's membrane away from the underlying stroma.
Place the strip into one well of a 6-well tissue culture plate coated with Attachment Factor containing 1 mL of culture medium.
Keep the lid on the tissue culture plate at all times, except when explants are being added.
Remove strips of Descemet’s membrane from the extreme periphery first and then from central regions later.
Place all strips from one cornea into a single well within the 6-well plate.
Incubate the explants in a humidified cell culture incubator set at 5% CO2 and 37 °C.
Leave the culture undisturbed for 2 days to allow the explants to settle and attach to the plate surface.
Remove the medium and any unattached explants from the culture after 4 days.
Gently add 2 mL of fresh culture medium, taking care not to disturb the attached explants.
Culture medium should be changed twice per week.
Place the explant culture onto the stage of a dissecting microscope and adjust illumination and zoom for visibility.
Gently pluck each explant from its culture plate using sterilized watchmaker forceps.
Transfer the explants to a fresh well of a 6-well tissue culture plate coated with Attachment Factor containing 1 mL of culture medium.
Allow the explants to settle on the surface of their new plate for 4 days before replacing the culture medium with 2 mL of fresh culture medium.
Change culture medium twice per week.
Sterilize round glass coverslips of 13 mm diameter in an autoclave or by soaking in 70% ethanol for 15 min followed by three rinses in phosphate-buffered saline (PBS).
Place individual sterilized coverslips into the wells of a 24-well tissue culture plate.
Coat the coverslips with Attachment Factor and add 0.5 mL of culture medium to each well.
Using sterilized watchmaker forceps, remove explants from their tissue culture plates.
Transfer explants to wells containing coverslips.
Allow explants to settle onto the coverslips for 4 days.
Change the medium after the required incubation period.
Fix and stain the coverslip cultures within their culture wells.
Mount stained coverslips onto glass microscope slides.
Analyze under a fluorescence microscope.
Remove the medium from the culture.
Briefly rinse with DPBS.
Add 1 mL of Versene to the wells.
Incubate at room temperature for 30 seconds.
Remove the Versene and add 1 mL of TrypLE.
Incubate at 37 °C in the tissue culture incubator for 3 minutes.
Observe the culture using a phase contrast microscope.
Gently tap the culture to dislodge cells from the plate.
Remove large fibroblastic cells and TrypLE with a 1 mL pipette.
Rinse remaining cells twice with 2 mL of DPBS.
Add 1 mL of 1 mg/mL Dispase II to the culture.
Incubate in the tissue culture incubator for 1 to 2 h or until all cells have detached from the plate.
Collect the detached cell clumps using a 1 mL pipette.
Transfer collected cells to 20 mL of DPBS in a 50 mL centrifuge tube.
Centrifuge at 300 x g for 5 min at room temperature.
Remove the supernatant and resuspend the cell pellet by trituration with a 1 mL pipette in 1 mL of culture medium.
Transfer the cell suspension to one or two wells of a 6-well plate, depending on the desired passage ratio (1:1 or 1:2).
Top up each well with 2 mL of medium and place cultures into the tissue culture incubator.
Replace the medium with 2 mL of fresh medium twice per week.
Assemble the upper chamber of the micro-Boyden chamber by placing a red O-ring into its center.
Punch out an 18 mm diameter disc from a biomaterial sheet using a trephine on a PTFE cutting board.
Place the punched-out disc over the red O-ring in the micro-Boyden chamber's upper chamber.
Screw the lower chamber onto the upper chamber, securing the biomaterial disc in between.
Soak the assembled micro-Boyden chamber in 70% ethanol for 1 h to sterilize it.
Completely immerse the assembled micro-Boyden chamber in sterile HBSS for 10 min to remove the ethanol.
Repeat this wash step twice with sterile HBSS.
Perform a final wash step for 10 min in unsupplemented culture medium.
Transfer the sterilized micro-Boyden chamber to culture medium in the well of a 6-well plate ensuring that the upper chamber is uppermost.
Adjust the level of culture medium so that it contacts the lower surface of the biomaterial membrane but does not flow into the upper chamber.
Prepare a suspension of corneal endothelial cells with a density of 500,000 cells per mL.
Pipette 100 µL of cell suspension onto the membrane in the micro-Boyden chamber.
Incubate the micro-Boyden chamber in the tissue culture incubator for 4 hours.
Top up the medium to completely submerge the chamber.
Incubate the culture, replacing the medium twice per week.
Flip over the micro-Boyden chamber within the culture well once cells have attached to the upper surface of the biomaterial membrane.
